clue.text: Iron-workers writing reports?

definitions.meaning: people who work a press, flattening or ironing material
journalists, the people of the press, who write news reports

explanation.surface: Steel-mill hands who moonlight as report writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron-workers' suggests steelmen; read it as people who press, as an iron does.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are people of the press: machine operators of a press, and newspaper journalists.

clue.text: A demonstrator paling

definitions.meaning: a striker standing outside a workplace in protest
a pointed stake forming part of a fence

explanation.definitionFit: A strike protester and a fence stake share the same word.

clue.text: The fellow getting a home surmounted by royal insignia

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed on top comes first, so the royal letters sit above the home

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A man moves into a house topped with the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's given name, so a particular fellow.

clue.text: Filmed in secret?

definitions.meaning: shown on screen, as a film is
hidden from view behind a screen

explanation.definitionFit: The same word means projected as a film and concealed behind a partition.

clue.text: Having set a spread, partakes of it

indicators.note: the letters of the words set and a are spread about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lays out a buffet and then tucks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges SET A into the answer, while the surface makes it a meal laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to partake of it.

clue.text: An American music composer's drink

definitions.meaning: Cole ..., American songwriter, with 's standing for 'is'
a dark beer once popular with market ...

explanation.surface: A drink named after an American songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter wrote American songs, and porter is a dark ale.

clue.text: Sort of street where people don't expect to meet any traffic

definitions.text: Sort of street where people don't expect to meet any traffic

parts.words: Sort of street where people don't expect to meet any traffic
parts.note: traffic all flows in the same direction, so nothing comes towards you head-on

explanation.definitionFit: On a street where vehicles travel in one direction only, no oncoming traffic is met.

clue.text: He's offered a small boat with some hesitation

parts.note: a tender is a small boat serving a larger vessel
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A man is offered a dinghy, but hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's offered' is read as 'he has offered': one who makes a formal bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderer is a person who submits a bid or offer.

clue.text: Member of the family presenting an account

definitions.meaning: the telling of a story, a narration

explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a relative, and recounting a tale is narration, both one word.

clue.text: Penitent cheat, quite well-known

parts.note: to con is to cheat
trite means hackneyed, so familiar as to be stale

explanation.surface: A swindler repents, which is a familiar story.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sorry for wrongdoing is remorseful, synonym for penitent.

clue.text: Five learn to make adjustment in spring

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: the letters of learn are adjusted into a different order

explanation.surface: Not many students adapt their studies in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make adjustment' rearranges LEARN into ERNAL after V; 'Few' as printed gives no V, so the page's word is read as 'Five'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal is the adjective for things belonging to the season of spring.

clue.text: The poet is no miser!

definitions.meaning: someone who lays out money freely, the opposite of a hoarder

explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was an English poet, and a person who spends freely is the opposite of a miser.

clue.text: Object about charge, so will be turned out

indicators.note: the object word goes round the charge word, surrounding it

parts.note: an end is an object or aim
to sue is to bring a charge in law

explanation.surface: An objection to a fee is raised, so someone will be ejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resulted or followed afterwards can be said to have happened as an outcome.

clue.text: Showing a person with children retains little money

indicators.note: the parent phrase holds on to the coin, keeping it inside

parts.note: a parent is someone with children
p, a penny, is a small British coin

explanation.surface: A parent keeps hold of some small change.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing here means visible or evident, which is what apparent describes.

clue.text: Prepared to fly

parts.note: what a bird did to its feathers to get ready for flight, also simply 'tidied oneself up'

explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom their plumage, and people smarten up, before setting off.

clue.text: Looking to keep on about Ireland

indicators.note: the persisting word wraps around the name for Ireland

parts.note: to peg away is to keep on working
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to keep talking about Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Peering is looking closely, a near synonym.

clue.text: A fine man-though he makes a woman duck!

parts.note: her refers to a woman
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A gallant gentleman, though he gets a lady to dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is a cricket score of zero, giving O; the surface wants it as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a brave, admirable man.

clue.text: They show sporting dogs

definitions.meaning: indicators or hints that point things out
a gun-dog breed that stands still to mark game

explanation.definitionFit: Signs that indicate are pointers, and so is a breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: A beast holding up a number is unfair

indicators.note: the beast word grips the number inside it

parts.note: a brute is a beast

indicators.note: in a down clue the number is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone says it is unfair that a beast is holding up a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TEN into NET, which 'holding' places inside BRUTE. 'unfair' means not fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette has dark hair, so is literally not fair in colouring.

clue.text: Settling deposit

parts.note: matter that sinks to the bottom of a liquid and collects there, not a payment

explanation.definitionFit: Particles that sink out of water and accumulate form a layer at the bottom.

clue.text: No Green party would have such a monster in

indicators.note: the words no green would have the creature contained in their letters

explanation.surface: An environmental party would never admit a beast to its ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would have' and the closing 'in' show the run inside No Green.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a giant monster of fairy tales.

clue.text: Upsetting reverse getting harder to endure

indicators.note: the letters of reverse are upset, thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A distressing setback that is getting worse to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more severe is harsher, so harder to bear.

clue.text: A deity in Nicaragua-the newest one

indicators.note: the goddess is found within the following words

explanation.surface: A god in Nicaragua, the latest one there.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene is the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: A holy man with some desire for physical discomfort

parts.note: St, saint, is a holy man
an itch is a desire

explanation.surface: A saint with some craving for bodily pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side.

clue.text: Mountain where a renegade accommodates gunmen

indicators.note: the renegade phrase takes in the gunmen, holding them inside

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or traitor
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A mountain where a turncoat shelters armed men.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the Turkish mountain where Noah's Ark came to rest.

clue.text: Another will complete the score

parts.note: a score is twenty, so this number is one short of it

explanation.definitionFit: One more on top of this number makes twenty, a score.

clue.text: The refuse issue

definitions.meaning: offspring, a brood of young animals

explanation.definitionFit: Scattered rubbish and a brood of puppies share the word.

clue.text: A supporter is provided with parking, and that is right

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A backer is given parking, and that's correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch.

clue.text: Admission to the course?

parts.note: right of entry, but also the dish served as a course of a meal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means right of entry, and it is also a dish served at dinner.

clue.text: A ball-game the sailor finds excellent

parts.note: fives is a British handball game played in a court
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman rates a handball game as superb.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hotel rating marks it as of the highest quality.

clue.text: Country quarters with a beautiful garden

parts.note: south and west are compass quarters
Eden is the paradise garden

explanation.surface: Rural lodgings with a lovely garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation.

clue.text: A note of whimsy

definitions.meaning: a musical note of one beat, a quarter note

explanation.definitionFit: A quarter note in music and an odd fancy share the word.
